newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate 13.5 vs 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate 13.5 vs 11.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate rose to 13.5 percent on Wednesday from 11.3 percent thanks to a higher volume of term loans.
Daily trade doubled to 47.4 million kuna, with supply topping demand by 22.6 million as banks' balances recovered after the government made provisions for salary payments.
But liquidity remained thin and the central bank said it might intervene to help the banking sector later in the week through a foreign exchange repurchase deal.
More than half of fresh borrowings were call money loans, struck at a weighted 11.1 percent, up 10 basis points from Wednesday.
Term rates varied between 9.0 percent charged by insurers for renewed deals and 13-18 percent for interbank loans.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Thursday eased to 6.1073 against the dollar and 3.5751 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
